title: Contrasting evidence on cover-crop biodiversity and water outcomes in drylands
authors: Multiple studies compiled as a conflict case
methodology: Intentionally paired findings used to test conflict handling: some dryland studies report soil-cover benefits, others report soil-water depletion and weak biodiversity response when cover crops transpire limited moisture.
limitations: This bundle is designed to surface disagreement; it is not a single experiment.

chunks.text: Study A reports that winter cover in semi-arid rotations can increase ground cover, reduce erosion, and contribute modest organic inputs, with associated increases in soil-surface habitat for invertebrates when biomass is achieved.

Study B reports that in low-rainfall systems, cover crops can reduce subsequent soil water and sometimes fail to produce enough biomass for biodiversity or carbon benefits. In those cases, a reliable percentage improvement in species richness should not be claimed.
